dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Ha, you're absolutely right. Nothing beats Mondstadt's Dandelion Wine.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: It's your long-awaited homecoming, so drink up — make the most of it. Oh, and while the Apple Cider and Dandelion Wine here are stellar, I must also recommend the cocktails. Death After Noon is a personal favorite.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: #Sound advice, Sir Kaeya. Let me see... Oh! {NICKNAME}! Can't believe we actually did run into each other here!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hearing that from you feels a bit... odd. The Honorary Knight of Favonius, welcoming a Mondstadter back home... Oh, don't mind me, haha...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: It's just... hard to describe. I'm happy, but also feeling a bit nostalgic. It's been so long.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And the things you had to take care of?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I already sorted through everything my mother left for me. Some were important documents, others old mementos, but everything was in good shape.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I also inspected and cleaned the house thoroughly. Old places that stay empty too long tend to start falling apart, after all — leaks here, cracks there.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I just finished that cleanup — it took way longer than I expected. Then I thought I'd pop out for some fresh air, and that's when I bumped into Sir Kaeya.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Mr. Thoma, you're always welcome here. The Honorary Knight isn't alone in being glad to see Ulrike's son return.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I'm sure you feel the same, hm?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Thank you both! Honestly, if I hadn't run into Sir Kaeya, I'd have struggled to even begin catching up on everything that's changed here.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Think nothing of it. Ulrike joined the Knights of Favonius before me, and it's my pleasure to assist her family.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Besides, I'm rather enjoying my time with you. Hearing a Mondstadter's firsthand account of Inazuma beats learning about it from reports any day.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: If you're interested in hearing more, maybe we can exchange addresses? There's a lot of things that can't be explained in a few words over drinks.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Gladly! Just address your letters to the Knights of Favonius. And on your end...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: You can send them to the Yashiro Commission in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Only half a day back home, and I've run into an old friend and met a new one who even knows my family...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: That's too much good fortune not to toast! Cheers! ... Ooh. Death After Noon... Now that's strong stuff...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Oh dear. Are you quite alright?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Um... I wish I could handle stronger liquor, but whew — I can already feel my face turning redder than a beet after just one glass.

choices.text: Have some non-alcoholic cider with me, then.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Surprising. Ulrike could drink most sailors under the table.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: ...Yeah, I remember tagging along with her to Knights of Favonius banquets. They were right here, at the Angel's Share.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Then, all the adults were drinking Dandelion Wine and Apple Cider, and I was the only one stuck drinking the non-alcoholic version. Drove me mad, too.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Ha! Let me guess what happened next: You snuck a taste of the "grown-up drinks"?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Busted. I swapped my glass with one of the adults, and... Ha. I recall being seated near the kitchen.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: What Mondstadt kid hasn't pulled that trick at least once? Diluc and I did something similar when we were children.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I knew it! There are some things only fellow Mondstadters really understand.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Anyway, that drink burned young me's throat like wildfire. Later, my mother sent some Apple Cider to Inazuma. I thought the taste might be mellower than I remembered, given it'd been so long...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Nope! Still burned all the way down. I ended up having to share the rest with the other Kamisato retainers, but they loved it.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Gave me a whole pile of gifts, too, which I sent back here along with my letter.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Huh. There was that time Ulrike was passing out Inazuman snacks to everyone... Is that why?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Maybe! Did you get to try any?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I did. Dango, I believe — good stuff, that. To whom at the Yashiro Commission do I owe my thanks?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: The dango... I think that was Miss Kamisato. Lord Kamisato sent tempura, Hirotatsu sent seasoned onigiri... Just two bottles for a whole smorgasbord of snacks!

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Well, like mother, like son. That was your kindness and enthusiasm being gifted back to you, I'd say.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: You may not have heard, but when your mother left for Nod-Krai, we Knights threw her a farewell party here.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: It was supposed to be a small event, but so many people attended that the place was packed. Take it from someone with firsthand experience.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Free-spirited and thoughtful, gentle and kind... Ulrike is the very model of a Knight.

choices.text: Looks like the apple doesn't fall far from your family's tree, Thoma.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: She'll be thrilled to hear that. Next time I write to her, I'll be sure to pass your kind words along.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Maybe toss in a bottle of good Inazuman sake... But for now, how about we switch to non-alcoholic cider?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Fine by me. A little variety never hurt anyone.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Between having heard your tales and making a new friend, this round's on me — yours included, Honorary Knight.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't mind if I do.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: By the way, Thoma, you never finished telling those youkai legends you mentioned before...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You, Thoma, and Kaeya talk of the tales of Inazuman youkai, and before you know it, the mugs of non-alcoholic cider Charles brought out have been drained dry.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Kitsune and bake-danuki making a bet? Haha, now that's a story!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Actually, it's not a story. It's true. If you should ever visit Inazuma, you can come find me at the Yashiro Commission.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I'll introduce you to real youkai. In Inazuma, whether oni or tengu, they work honest jobs like everyone else.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I'm already looking forward to it. Today's drinking session has been most fruitful.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Then it's settled. I expect they'll all be thrilled to have you as their new friend.

choices.text: Looks like you're all getting on great.
Be sure to come back when you get the chance.
I'd say being in Mondstadt agrees with you.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Absolutely. The windmills, the Archon statue in the square, and Mom's favorite tavern...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Everything's exactly like I remembered, the same as in my dreams. It's wonderful.
